root_cause.text: In __smc_setsockopt() (net/smc/af_smc.c), a user-space memory copy (copy_from_sockptr) is performed while the socket lock is held, allowing an attacker to block indefinitely by providing userfaultfd- or FUSE-backed memory, thus holding the lock and causing a local denial of service.
root_cause.evidence: The patch moves the copy_from_sockptr call from inside the lock_sock(sk) critical section to before acquiring the lock, preventing the sleep-inducing copy from blocking while the lock is held. The CVE description explicitly states that passing userfaultfd-monitored memory as optval causes the copy to halt, keeping the lock held and triggering watchdog and workqueue exhaustion.

intent_record.intent_summary: Pre-fetch user data for SMC_LIMIT_HS option outside the socket lock to minimize lock hold time and fail early on invalid input.
intent_record.what: Moved the copy of user data (optval) and validation of optlen for the SMC_LIMIT_HS setsockopt option from inside the lock_sock() critical section to before acquiring the lock, and changed error handling to early returns instead of setting rc and breaking.
intent_record.how: The change reduces the time the socket lock is held by performing the copy_from_sockptr() and length check before lock_sock(). If the input is invalid or copying fails, the function returns an error immediately without ever acquiring the lock, avoiding unnecessary lock contention.
